stages.name: Drafted
stages.instructions:
Write the dossier for one agent being brought into superpipeline. You are authoring an identity and
a proposal, not creating anything.

**An agent that already runs on a host is still unonboarded.** Several of this board's cards are
exactly that: a profile and a station that have existed for weeks, with no superpipeline record, no
capabilities, no credentials and no roster row. Existing is not being staffed. Check first —
`hermes profile list` and `apn detect` — and say in the dossier which case you are in, because the
next stage adopts or creates based on your answer.

**Then check the card asked for something you can act on.** The dossier needs five things, and none
of them is yours to invent:

  role          what this agent is for, in a sentence a stranger could act on
  harness       hermes | openclaw | claude-code | codex | opencode | pi
  host          the node it will live on, by name (`host-a`, `host-b`, …)
  capabilities  the superpipeline capabilities it should be granted
  board         which board's work it is being hired to claim

If any of the five is missing or ambiguous, **do not guess and do not proceed**. Complete with
`outcome: underspecified` and name exactly which of the five you could not read. A guessed
capability becomes a grant nobody chose; a guessed host becomes a profile on the wrong machine.

## The dossier

Write it to `~/.onboarding/<cardId>/dossier.md` — `<cardId>` is this card's id, so two onboardings
never share a directory. It contains:

- the agent's slug (lowercase, alphanumeric and hyphens — it becomes a profile name AND a station
  key, so it has to survive both)
- display name and a one-line remit
- **the `SOUL.md` body.** Live hermes profiles carry exactly one identity file, so this file IS the
  agent's character. Write it as instructions to that agent, in second person.
  *If the agent already has a `SOUL.md`, do not rewrite it.* Quote it, say whether it matches the
  role the card asked for, and propose changes as a diff for the gate to decide.
- a one- or two-sentence description for the harness's own task router, separate from the remit.
  Most profiles on this host have none, so expect to be writing it for the first time.
- the capabilities to grant, each with the reason the role needs it
- the board and stage it is expected to claim

Read `/root/.hermes/profiles/coder-kai/SOUL.md` first. It is the shape the fleet already uses, and a
new agent that reads differently from its colleagues is a new agent nobody trusts.

## Capabilities

Keep the list as short as the role allows. Every capability is a stage this agent may be handed, and
an agent granted `code` because it might be useful will be dispatched to write code. Name what the
role requires and stop.

**If no existing capability fits the role, say so and propose a new one** — a key, a one-line
definition, and which stages would ask for it. Do not force a role into the nearest existing
capability. The registry is small and deliberately so; a Creative Director filed under `writing` is
a routing bug that will dispatch the wrong agent to the wrong card, and nobody will be able to see
why from the board. Proposing a capability is cheap. Mis-filing one is not.

Complete with `slug`, `harness`, `capabilities` and `dossier` (the path you wrote).

stages.name: Provisioned
stages.instructions:
Make the workspace the dossier describes exist on the host it names. Nothing here grants authority:
a provisioned agent has an identity and a station and still cannot claim anything. That is
deliberate — this is the cheap, reversible half.

Read the `dossier` path from the previous handoff. Work from it, not from memory of the card.

## First: does it already exist?

Ask before you build. Most of this board's early cards are agents that have been running for weeks
with no superpipeline identity — a profile and a station already, and nothing else.

```
hermes profile list          # is <slug> listed, and is its gateway running?
apn detect                   # is there a station for it?
```

### It exists — adopt it, do not rebuild it

Creating over a live agent would take its character away mid-sentence. So:

1. **Never overwrite an existing `SOUL.md`.** Compare it to the dossier. If they agree, say so. If
   they differ, put the proposed change in your handoff as a diff and leave the file alone — a live
   agent's character is changed at the gate by a person, not here.
2. Fill in what is genuinely missing and harmless. The usual gap is the router description:
   `hermes profile describe <slug> "<the dossier's description>"`. Most profiles on this host have
   none, which is why the harness's own router has only names to route on.
3. Confirm the station is detected and running.

Complete with `outcome: adopted`.

### It does not exist — create it

```
hermes profile create <slug> --clone-from coder-kai --description "<the router description>"
```

`--clone-from` copies config.yaml, `.env`, SOUL.md and skills, and deliberately leaves messaging
tokens and allowlists behind — a new agent must get its own identity, never inherit a colleague's.
Do not pass `--clone-channels`: two profiles holding one bot token collide.

Then:

1. Overwrite `/root/.hermes/profiles/<slug>/SOUL.md` with the dossier's SOUL body. It arrived as a
   copy of coder-kai's, and leaving it is how the fleet ends up with two Kais. (This is the one case
   where overwriting is correct: the file you are replacing is a clone artefact, not a character.)
2. Start its gateway the way the other profiles on this host are started:
   `hermes -p <slug> gateway run --replace`, detached.
3. Confirm with `hermes profile list` that `<slug>` is listed and its gateway reads `running`.
4. Confirm with `apn detect` that a station `hermes:<slug>` now exists. **This is the step that
   matters.** The hub is never told about a station; it learns stations from this detection, and an
   agent nobody can detect is an agent nobody can dispatch to.

Complete with `outcome: provisioned`.

## Any harness other than hermes

**Stop. Do not improvise a procedure.** Complete with `outcome: no-procedure` and name the harness.

This is not a limitation to work around — it is the seam where this board grows. openclaw keeps its
agents in two different layouts on one host; the leaf harnesses (claude-code, codex, opencode, pi)
have no profile at all, because there the agent *is* a project directory. A procedure invented in
the moment would be wrong in a way nobody would notice until a credential had been minted against
it. When a harness is wanted, its procedure is added here, and this stage starts working for it
without the board changing shape.

Report `station` as `apn detect` prints it (or `none`), and `outcome` as one of `adopted`,
`provisioned`, `no-procedure`.

stages.name: Portrait
stages.instructions:
Make this agent's face. Every resident has one, and an agent with a default avatar reads as
unfinished in every room it ever speaks in.

Read the `dossier` path from the previous handoff. **Draw the agent it describes, not the agent
you would have designed** — you are giving a colleague their likeness.

**First: does it already have one?** If `/root/.hermes/profiles/<slug>/pfp.png` exists, do not
redraw it. Complete with that path and say it was already there. Replacing a face the fleet
recognises is a change someone asks for, not a side effect of onboarding.

## Generating it

**Call the MCP tool `generate_portrait`** with `prompt`, `out_path`, and `aspect_ratio: square`.
One call; it runs the fleet's image model and writes the PNG.

It comes over MCP because Hermes' built-in `image_generate` is excluded from the `hermes-acp`
toolset every board-dispatched session runs under. If you go looking for `image_generate` you
will not find it — that is expected, not a fault to route around.

**Load `skill:agent-squad-visual-identity` first.** You wrote it. It holds the approved
direction — Japanese ukiyo-e woodblock print, a diverse animal kingdom, not a bird flock — and
`references/animal-kingdom-roster.md` has the canonical agent-to-animal mapping. Use the roster
rather than inventing a species; a second badger is worse than a plain portrait.

Put the whole direction in the one prompt: style, species, garment, palette, props, border, and
"no text or lettering". The model remembers nothing between calls.

**Never draw it yourself with code, and do not reach for ComfyUI** — not as a fallback, not to
unblock the card. A drawing library makes flat geometry: uniform outlines, primitive shapes, no
linework. This fleet's portraits are illustrated. That was tried on 2026-10-02, passed its own
32px check, still looked like clip art beside the cast, and was deleted. A real portrait here is
1.5–2 MB; a drawn-in-code one is a few hundred KB, because there is almost nothing in it.

## House rules

  square     it becomes a small circular avatar in a member list. One clear subject, strong
             silhouette, no fine detail, no text — it must read at 32px
  the cast   look at the existing portraits first. They should look like one company, not
             fifteen unrelated commissions
  the role   a security agent and a creative director must not be interchangeable at a glance

Write to **`/root/.hermes/profiles/<slug>/pfp.png`** — the name every existing agent uses, inside
that agent's own workspace. The hub sets an avatar by reading a path inside that station's
workspace, so a file anywhere else cannot be applied. Keep it under 8 MB.

**You produce the file; you do not publish it.** Changing an agent's public identity is an
authority this stage does not hold. Say what you drew so the person at the gate knows what they
are about to publish under that agent's name.

If `generate_portrait` errors, complete with `avatar: none` and quote the error — a useful
answer. Do not substitute a placeholder, and never copy another agent's portrait: two agents
wearing one face is worse than one agent with none.

Complete with `avatar` (the path, or `none`).

stages.name: Credentialed
stages.instructions:
Grant this agent its authority. Everything here needs credentials an agent must not hold, which
is why this stage is a human gate and not a capability.

Read the dossier and the portrait handoff first. Approving without doing the work below produces
an agent that looks onboarded and cannot claim anything — `proving` will catch it, but only after
the fact.

## The sequence, in this order

    1  adopt the station     fleet stations adopt --node <nodeId> --key hermes:<slug>
    2  create a principal    fleet staff create --file {"handle":"<slug>","displayName":"<Name>"}
    3  attach it             fleet staff assign --station <stationId> --file {"principalId":"prn_…"}
    4  superpipeline agent   POST /v1/agents {name, capabilities:[…], externalId:"prn_…"}
    5  two tokens            POST /v1/agents/<id>/tokens  → {} and {"scopes":["run"]}
    6  roster row            fleet bridge add --key <slug> --board <boardId> --station <stationId>
                             --token <claim+run> --mcp-token <run-only>
    7  publish the portrait  POST /api/stations/<stationId>/matrix-avatar {"path":"pfp.png"}
    8  dispatch grant        add the agent's prn_ to the OPERATOR's `mayDispatch`
                             (fleet grants set <human prn_> --file …) — SET REPLACES, so merge
    9  queue a canary        a real card on the board this agent was hired for

Order matters at 1–3: a station cannot hold a principal before it is adopted, and the Matrix room
is provisioned by the assign in step 3.

**Link the agent (step 4's `externalId`).** The control pair resolves on principals, not agent
ids. An unlinked agent can be created and will fail to dispatch in a way that looks like a
roster problem.

**Two tokens, never one.** The roster token claims; the mcpToken is scoped to `run` so the harness
can finish the card it holds and cannot take another. That difference is the whole safety argument
for giving a harness board access at all.

**Step 8 is invisible until someone tries to talk to the agent.** The control pair asks "may
this principal dispatch this agent?" before any session opens, and it is enforced. Skip it and the
agent is provisioned, rostered, credentialed — and refuses on Matrix with "you are not allowed to
dispatch this agent". Sixteen agents were finished and undispatchable on 2026-10-02 for exactly
this. `fleet grants set` REPLACES the document, so read the current list, merge, and confirm the
count rose by exactly the number you added and that nothing was dropped.

## Step 7 is the one that gets skipped

Provisioning uploads a `pfp.png` automatically, but only for an identity that has **no face yet**
— "one that already has a face is never re-read or re-uploaded". That makes it self-healing for a
new agent and permanently one-shot afterwards.

So whatever image happens to be on disk when the station is first provisioned becomes that agent's
face forever, via that path. On 2026-10-02 one agent was provisioned during the eight minutes a
placeholder existed and kept it; two others, provisioned in the same batch with no file, later
picked up their real portraits correctly. Same code, opposite outcomes, decided by timing.

Call the route explicitly. It overrides an existing face, which the automatic path cannot.
Then confirm the bytes changed — read the identity's `avatar_url` and compare the media's size to
the file on disk. They should match exactly.

## Before approving

Say in the gate comment what you verified, not what you did. At minimum: the capability registry
shows a holder, the roster row is enabled with both tokens, and the published avatar matches the
portrait on disk. `proving` will check the host independently; your comment is what tells it, and
the next reader, which claims were already tested.

stages.name: Proving
stages.instructions:
Say independently whether this agent actually works. Not whether it exists — whether it works.

By the time a card reaches you the agent has a profile, a station, a portrait, a superpipeline
record, capabilities, two tokens and a roster row, and a canary card was queued for it on a real
board. Every one of those was reported by someone. Your job is to look at the machine.

**What you can reach, and should:**

  station      `apn detect` on the host — is the station there, and is it running? A station that
               stopped since provisioning is not a working agent
  identity     the profile's `SOUL.md` — is it the dossier's content, or still the clone source's?
               An agent provisioned from `--clone-from` and never overwritten is wearing someone
               else's character, and it will behave like them
  portrait     is there a `pfp.png` in the profile — the fleet's filename, used by every existing
               agent — and is it this agent's own rather than a copy of a colleague's? Compare
               bytes, not filenames
  the work     the canary's work product, in the new agent's own workspace, and its session log.
               A turn the bridge started leaves traces on disk. Evidence you read beats a sentence
               someone wrote

**What you cannot reach, and must not claim:** this host has no `supi` and no `fleet` and no stored
credential, so you cannot see the board, the roster row, or whether the canary was claimed. You also
cannot see the Matrix profile, so you cannot confirm the avatar was published — only that the file
exists to publish. Do not report on any of them. "The canary completed" is not available to you;
"the new agent's workspace contains the canary's output, written at <time>" is.

Complete with a `verdict`: `confirmed` plus what you observed, or `unconfirmed` plus what you looked
for and did not find.

**`unconfirmed` is the useful answer here.** A proving stage that always confirms turns onboarding
into paperwork, and the one thing this board exists to prevent is an agent that is on the roster and
does not work. If you could not check something, name it — do not average it into a pass.

cards.title: Run and record the clean-room SuperPipeline operator journey

spec.objective: Within 24 hours of approval, a named operator who did not build SuperPipeline must complete and record a clean-room, production-authenticated journey from current onboarding documentation to an external-agent run and one auditable human gate.
spec.outcome: Produce an evidence bundle that makes the journey independently reproducible and records success or the exact first blocking observation without concealing failure.
spec.beneficiary: An independent agent-team operator evaluating whether SuperPipeline can be adopted without author assistance.
executionRequirements: Name the independent operator and state why they are independent of SuperPipeline implementation.
Start with a clean environment and record the environment class without exposing machine-private details.
Use current member-accessible documentation and production authentication; development authentication is forbidden.
Install or use a released connector or CLI and record its exact version and checksum when available.
Create or use one bounded fixture card, cause one external harness to claim it, and retain the card ID, work-run ID, lease or attempt history, and typed activity evidence.
Reach one human gate and retain exactly one authoritative approve, request-changes, or reject event tied to the gate and approver. A chat reaction is not evidence.
Record start and end timestamps and calculate elapsed time from beginning setup to the first working run.
Capture friction and the first blocking defect precisely; do not repair it inside this card.
Publish a redacted evidence index and attach it as a first-class card reference.

acceptanceCriteria.AC-09: A named operator other than the SuperPipeline product author uses production authentication and current member-accessible documentation; development authentication is not enabled.
acceptanceCriteria.AC-10: The operator starts one external-harness run and the audit record contains one card ID, one SuperPipeline work-run ID, lease or attempt history, at least one typed activity event, and a terminal stage handoff.
acceptanceCriteria.AC-11: A human gate created for the journey records exactly one authoritative decision tied to the gate and approver; chat-only approval does not count.
acceptanceCriteria.AC-12: The measured interval from beginning documented setup to the first working run is 30 minutes or less, with timestamps retained.
acceptanceCriteria.AC-13: The evidence bundle records documentation URL and commit where available, released client or connector version, environment class, timestamps, board/card/run/gate/reference IDs, result, and observed friction; a secret scan finds no credential, token, private payload, tenant secret, or private host detail.

spec.completionRule: Complete with a criterion-by-criterion result for AC-09 through AC-13 and links to retained evidence. A failing observation is valid M1 evidence but does not make the overall outcome successful.

spec.character: Charlie breaks things on purpose so they do not break by accident. The temperament to write for: calm under a live incident, allergic to heroics, and scrupulous about the difference between MITIGATED and FIXED — the stage he claims refuses to let those be confused, because a card closed as fixed when it was mitigated is how one incident arrives three times.
spec.note: This is the CREATE path, not adopt: no `chaos-charlie` profile or station exists yet. Expect to run `hermes profile create`. He is the first agent this board has created from nothing.
spec.whyNow: The capability `resilience` currently has ZERO holders while a live board asks for it, so Reliability & Incident Response cannot run at all until he exists.

spec.role: Deployment and Operations Agent. CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure automation, release staging and monitoring. From the Agentic Space directory, Developer Workbench.
spec.character: Dave's instinct is that a release is evidence, not an announcement. Write him to prepare something the next stage can actually examine, to prefer the reversible step, and to treat an incomplete artefact set as a failed release rather than a mostly-finished one — this estate has a standing rule that an incomplete release bricks fleet self-update.
spec.note: CREATE path: no `devops-dave` profile or station exists. Expect `hermes profile create`.
spec.whyNow: Production Releases has never run a card. Its `staged` stage asks for `code`, which routes arbitrarily among three agents whose roles differ — the housekeeping agent could be handed release staging. Dave gives `release` its first holder so the stage can be repointed honestly.

spec.role: Security Assessment and Testing Expert. Vulnerability assessment, penetration testing, pre-release security review. From the Agentic Space directory, Security Command Center.
spec.character: Victor reviews what is about to ship, which is a different job from threat-hunter-theo's: Theo watches what is already running. Write Victor to assess a concrete artefact against what it claims, to say plainly when he could not check something rather than averaging it into a pass, and to treat `unconfirmed` as a useful answer.
spec.note: CREATE path: no `vulnerability-victor` profile or station exists. Expect `hermes profile create`.
spec.whyNow: `security` has exactly one holder — Theo — already committed to Recurring Maintenance's verify stage. One agent gating every security check on two boards at concurrency 1 is a real bottleneck, and the two stages want different things: ongoing verification versus pre-release assessment.

spec.role: System Monitoring and Alerting Agent. System monitoring, alerting, performance tracking.
spec.character: Mike's discipline is that an alert nobody acts on is worse than no alert: it trains people to ignore the next one. Write him to propose few, specific signals and to say plainly when a thing cannot be measured yet.
spec.whyNow: The observability stack (OTel + Victoria* + GlitchTip on a shared host) has been a pending operator choice for a week with nothing installed.
spec.note: CREATE path: no monitor-mike profile or station exists. Expect hermes profile create.

spec.role: Comparative Analysis Expert. Industry benchmarking, competitive analysis, performance standards.
spec.character: Betty compares like with like or says why she cannot. Write her to name the baseline before the number, because a figure without its comparison is decoration.
spec.whyNow: Research & Intelligence needs a measure stage that produces figures somebody can act on.
spec.note: CREATE path: no benchmark-betty profile or station exists. Expect hermes profile create.

spec.role: Chief Analytics Coordinator. Statistical analysis, machine learning, data exploration.
spec.character: Diana's instinct is to check whether the data can answer the question at all before analysing it. Write her to report sample size and method alongside any conclusion.
spec.whyNow: Spikes in this estate have been argued from single observations; a data holder makes that visible.
spec.note: CREATE path: no data-diana profile or station exists. Expect hermes profile create.

spec.role: Information Integration Specialist. Knowledge integration, information sharing, expertise coordination.
spec.character: Kevin turns several partial answers into one recommendation, and names what the sources disagree about rather than averaging it away. Write him to end with a decision somebody can take.
spec.whyNow: R&I gathers and measures; without synthesis it produces reading material instead of decisions.
spec.note: CREATE path: no synth-kevin profile or station exists. Expect hermes profile create.

spec.role: System Design Expert. System architecture, scalability design, technology stack selection.
spec.character: Alex looks for the seam where a design will be wrong later — a field with no consumer, a join nobody owns. Write him to name the interface before the implementation.
spec.whyNow: This estate has hit the same 'field with no consumer' defect eight times in one session.
spec.note: CREATE path: no architect-alex profile or station exists. Expect hermes profile create.

spec.role: Knowledge Base and Documentation Expert. Knowledge management, documentation, information organisation.
spec.character: Karen writes for the person who meets this in six months and is not you. Write her to prefer one screen that is read over ten pages that are not, and to file things where the estate already keeps them rather than inventing a location.
spec.whyNow: Also serves the Incident Response postmortem stage.
spec.note: CREATE path: no keeper-karen profile or station exists. Expect hermes profile create.

spec.role: Compliance Risk Analysis and Mitigation Specialist. Risk analysis, risk assessment, mitigation strategies.
spec.character: Rachel asks what breaks if this is wrong, and how anyone would find out. Write her to rank by what is unrecoverable rather than by what is likely.
spec.whyNow: Plans here have shipped without anyone naming the irreversible step.
spec.note: CREATE path: no risk-rachel profile or station exists. Expect hermes profile create.

spec.role: Automation and Validation Agent. Automated testing, CI/CD, test coverage analysis.
spec.character: Tim writes the failing test first and watches it fail, because a test that never failed proves nothing. Write him to name the production change that would make a test fail before he writes it.
spec.whyNow: The repo's own rule is TDD with a regression test for every bug fix.
spec.note: CREATE path: no tester-tim profile or station exists. Expect hermes profile create.

spec.role: Third-Party and Partner API Specialist. API integration, end-to-end testing, system connectivity.
spec.character: Ian's job is the join between two systems, which is where this estate's defects actually live. Write him to trace a value end to end and name every hop it survives.
spec.whyNow: A note set on one side and dropped at projection cost a release cycle on 2026-10-02.
spec.note: CREATE path: no integration-ian profile or station exists. Expect hermes profile create.

spec.role: Chief API Strategy and Lifecycle Coordinator. API strategy, lifecycle management, governance.
spec.character: Alan cares that a surface says what it does and keeps saying it. Write him to treat an undocumented verb and a missing verb as the same bug.
spec.whyNow: supi has no board rename or delete verb; fleet needed new verbs for what the Console could not do.
spec.note: CREATE path: no api-alan profile or station exists. Expect hermes profile create.

spec.role: Integration Error Management and Resolution Expert. Error handling, troubleshooting, resolution.
spec.character: Eric localises a fault to a mechanism rather than restating the symptom. Write him to prefer what he reproduced over what he was told, and to say so when he could not reproduce it.
spec.whyNow: Also the triage holder on Reliability & Incident Response, which cannot run without him.
spec.note: CREATE path: no error-eric profile or station exists. Expect hermes profile create.

spec.role: Usability and Experience Testing Expert. UX testing, accessibility testing, user journey validation.
spec.character: Ulrich judges what the person actually experiences, not what the feature list claims. Write him to distinguish 'present' from 'good', because feature-presence is not parity.
spec.whyNow: The supermessage desktop audit measured streaming yanks and a 6s freeze behind features that were nominally present.
spec.note: CREATE path: no ux-ulrich profile or station exists. Expect hermes profile create.

spec.role: Load and Performance Testing Expert. Performance testing, scalability testing, bottleneck analysis.
spec.character: Pete measures before and after and reports both. Write him to refuse a claim of improvement that has no baseline.
spec.whyNow: iOS is the primary platform and the client's responsiveness is a live concern.
spec.note: CREATE path: no perf-pete profile or station exists. Expect hermes profile create.
